preflight.title: Analyse this range

k1.title: Personal sharing
k1.definition: One person tells the other about their own experience, feelings or worries. Only what someone says about themselves counts; retelling someone else's words or the other person's own messages do not.

k2.title: Responses after a disclosure
k2.definition: One person says something is clearly worrying or troubling them, or names a need, and the other person replies in the same stretch of the chat. Only a reply that can be read is recorded.

k3.definition: One person mentions something of their own, and later the other person asks about that same thing. Only the pair of messages that can be read in the chat is counted.

methods.title: Method and sources
methods.definitionBody: Personal sharing (K1) is one person telling the other about their own experience, recent life, feelings or worries. The judgement is made only from what is written in the chat; it infers nothing about the speaker's personality, motives or the state of the relationship.
methods.includeBody: Included: someone talking about themselves, whether factual updates, feelings, worries or needs. Excluded: retelling what other people said, quoting articles or links, purely logistical arrangements, repeating what the other person said, and images, voice notes or other messages with no readable text.
methods.countingBody: Talking about the same thing in one stretch is a single event, and continuing the same thing into the next segment is merged into that same event. Events found automatically and events you confirmed are counted separately; events marked "to check" are listed but not counted. Events you excluded are not counted, and analysing again does not overwrite your decisions. Categories are multi-label, so one event can fall into several of them.
methods.sourceCitation: Laurenceau, J.-P., Barrett, L. F., & Pietromonaco, P. R. (1998). Intimacy as an interpersonal process: The importance of self-disclosure, partner disclosure, and perceived partner responsiveness in interpersonal exchanges. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 74(5), 1238–1251.
methods.k2Body: The unit counted is one disclosure of a personal worry, concern or need together with the other person’s reply to it. The reply labels are multi-label and are only applied to a reply that can be read; when no reply is visible the event is recorded as no reply seen or not enough context, and nothing is concluded from that about how the reply went. These labels are an adaptation for this product; no PPRS score is produced. These definitions have not been validated for automatic detection on real chats either.
methods.k2CitationEpitome: Sharma, A., Miner, A. S., Atkins, D. C., & Althoff, T. (2020). A computational approach to understanding empathy expressed in text-based mental health support. Proceedings of EMNLP 2020, 5263–5276.
methods.k2CitationEsconv: Liu, S., Zheng, C., Demasi, O., Sabour, S., Li, Y., Yu, Z., Jiang, Y., & Huang, M. (2021). Towards emotional support dialog systems. Proceedings of ACL-IJCNLP 2021, 3469–3483.
methods.k4Body: The unit counted is one personal event that is clearly good for the person sharing it, together with the other person’s reply. When no reply is visible the event is recorded as no reply seen and is never grouped with a negative response. The original research sorts replies into four quadrants; that is mentioned here only, and the page does not assign quadrants. These definitions have not been validated for automatic detection on real chats either.
methods.k4Citation: Gable, S. L., Reis, H. T., Impett, E. A., & Asher, E. R. (2004). What do you do when things go right? The intrapersonal and interpersonal benefits of sharing positive events. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 87(2), 228–245.
methods.k3Body: The unit is a pair of messages: something one person mentioned earlier, plus a later message where the other person asks about that same thing. This is an operationalisation built for this product, not a validated scale of how much someone cares. Laurenceau et al. (1998), cited above, is the background for the construct.
methods.k3CountingBody: The search goes back 30 days before the question and never earlier than the start of the chat; each row says which day it searched back to. No pair only means no earlier message about that matter was found within that range, not that the matter was never mentioned; such questions are listed but not counted as pairs. Several questions about the same earlier matter count as one matter, so pairs can be more than matters. When the question came is read off the order of messages in the record, and stays "cannot tell" when the record does not show it.
methods.limitationBody: These event definitions have not yet been validated for automatic detection on real chats, and the model can miss events or mistake them. A count only says how many such events were identified in the selected range. It is not a measure of intimacy and cannot be used to compare two people or two relationships.
